item.content:encoded:
there seems to be this pervasive attitude that nobody should enjoy it because reasons I don't enjoy it on a lot of his stuff.

That's the beauty of unspecific broadsides. You get to put words in the mouths of people you disagree with since you don't specifically name anyone or any critique in particular. Feel free to point out where in any of my reviews I say those things. Unless your point is that critiquing something is claiming that "nobody should enjoy it," in which case, come out and say that and we can at least have an honest discussion.

I imagine it's got to be tiring for daveyoufool to have to try and politely address the same complaints on his -J SCPs that are clearly being enjoyed by a lot of other readers.

That's the thing about putting out work at high volume. You get a high volume of comments. There is nothing requiring daveyoufool to respond to any of it, and the extent of his commentary here seems to be "I understand what you're saying, but I'm going to continue doing things this way." Which is totally fine. That's his prerogative as a writer. Just as it's my prerogative as a reader to point out issues as I see them. Also, so what if something is enjoyed by a lot of other readers? Does that mean stuff with positive ratings over a certain threshold become immune to criticism? That's completely absurd.

Kind of like how people enjoy Tyler Perry movies, despite the fact that there are plenty of detractors who feel like he shouldn't make movies anymore

This "people who criticize these articles are saying daveyoufool shouldn't write anymore" straw man is disingenuous. Either cite some specific commentary so that we can address that, or stop trotting it out.

even though they aren't the target audience at all

The idea of a target audience in the context of a collaborative writing site where everyone's work is interrelated to varying degrees is a little tricky, and certainly more complicated than the premise of "well if you don't like it then just don't read it." Regardless of any of that, none of us get to pick and choose our readership.

I laughed at this article. Multiple times. So I upvoted it.

Good for you. I don't recall advocating specifically for people to not upvote this or not enjoy it. I'm not sure why you're so defensive about liking this article.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I think a relevant question when considering the appropriateness of negative feedback on this type of article is "Why do people write for this site?"

If this is primarily an entertainment thing, where the aim is to give the readers a sugar-high of recognition and reaffirmation, then perhaps it's correct to say that some articles are exempt from criticism, "it's just a summer blockbuster"-style.

If participation on the site is primarily for the purpose of collaboratively improving our writing craft, then I think it's absolutely legitimate to comment on everything that is submitted, even if the same comments are being repeated, even if the work has "good box office" in upvotes.

The truth lies in between, of course. But I think that the chances of readers being charmed by being pandered to (as opposed to the quality of the work) is particularly high for self-referential subject matter. And it's fair to make comment on that fact, as there is a path from there to self-congratulation and self-indulgence on the part of the site. Here, my view is that the craft is not particularly strong, and that while the concept could work, it is an easy enough target that it deserves to be written better.

And I don't think anyone should be exempt from receiving criticism along the same vein in multiple works, if the same issues are present. Often dave exhibits stronger technique and gets greater effect, and I'll upvote that, even if there is a Spanko reference. But relying on Spanko references too much can itself be bad craft - like catchphrases in sitcoms.

One final point where I want to give credit to dave. I was quite critical a while back about the formulaic nature of many of his submissions. Since then, almost none of his works has relied on that formula - they've taken a variety of other approaches to get laughs. That is good craft, and to his credit.
